intro: To download a Google Sheet as Excel on a Mac, open the File menu, choose Download, then pick Microsoft Excel (.xlsx). Your browser saves the file to your Downloads folder, and you can open it in Excel for Mac or another spreadsheet app.
tldr: Click File, hover over Download, then choose Microsoft Excel (.xlsx).
The browser saves the file to Downloads. Open it in Excel for Mac, then check the formulas.
Google's Mac shortcut list has no shortcut for Download as Excel. Use the menu.
A greyed-out Download option usually means you have Viewer or Commenter access. Ask the owner for Editor access.

blocks.text: Google Sheets is a web app. You open it in a browser, and the download option sits inside that browser window. Google's help pages say the File menu on a Mac is the same as on Windows, so these steps carry over.
Check your access before you start

Your role on the file decides whether the download works. Owners and Editors can download. Google's developer documentation says that when the viewer and commenter restriction is on, readers and commenters cannot download, print, or copy the file.
Open the file and check how it was shared with you. If you see View or Comment, ask the owner for Editor access. Copying the data by hand is slower, and it can drop formatting and formulas.
Why Google's wording and the guides disagree
Google's official help page on Excel and Sheets says to click File, then Download as, then select the file format you want. That page does not name Microsoft Excel in that step.
Google's export help page maps Excel's Save As to Sheets' Download. So the menu names differ a little, but the idea is the same. You are saving the spreadsheet in Excel's format.

Some third-party guides write the path as File > Download > Microsoft Excel (.xlsx). One Mac guide from The Bricks, dated February 3, 2025, uses that path. Read the submenu on your screen and pick the Excel option by name.
Where the downloaded file lands on your Mac
Your browser saves the file to the Downloads folder on your Mac. Open Finder, click Downloads in the sidebar, and look for a file that ends in .xlsx. The name usually matches the spreadsheet title.
If you cannot find it, open your browser's download list first. It shows where the file went. Then try the download again if it is missing.
Leave the file in Downloads until you have checked it. Move it to a project folder after that, so you always know which copy you tested.
Check the Excel file before you share it
A download is a copy, not a live link. Once the .xlsx leaves Google Sheets, edits in Excel stay in Excel. Later changes in Sheets will not reach that file.
Formulas need a look. The Bricks guide says QUERY functions and some Sparklines may not convert. Find those cells in Excel and look for errors or blank results.

Some third-party guides say every tab comes across in one download. Google's own help pages do not confirm this. Count the tabs in Excel and compare them with the Sheets file before you delete anything.
Limits that can shrink or block your export

Google Sheets files have size limits. Google's Drive help says a spreadsheet can hold up to 20 million cells or 100 MB. A Google Workspace Updates post dated September 10, 2026 raised the cell limit from 10 million to 20 million.

That change covers new, existing and imported files. Google's post says there is no admin control and no end-user setting for it. Older guides still quote 10 million cells, so trust the current Google source.

Drive help also says that when a file is converted, any cell with more than 50,000 characters is removed in Sheets. Check long text cells, such as pasted notes or logs, before you export. Shorten them or move the text elsewhere.
Connected Sheets pivot tables work under their own caps. Drive help limits those pivot tables to 200k rows. If you rely on a connected pivot, check its row count before you download the file.
Shortcuts that help on a Mac, and the one that is missing
Google's Mac shortcut list includes a few keys that matter here. Ctrl+Option+F, written ⌃⌥F, opens the File menu. ⌘P opens Print. ⌘S saves, although Sheets saves to Drive on its own as you work.
The same list has no shortcut for Download, and none for Make a copy. So the Excel download needs the mouse or trackpad. Open the File menu with ⌃⌥F, then move down to Download.
Need a PDF instead of Excel? Use File > Print, or ⌘P. The print window offers Workbook, Selected cells and Current sheet. Pick one, then click Next.
Chrome shows a print window. Firefox and Safari download a PDF file on their own. Pick the format that matches what you need to send.
What to do when Download is greyed out
A greyed-out Download option usually points to access. The Bricks guide says it usually means your account lacks Editor access. It also says owners can turn off downloads for viewers and commenters.

Google's developer documentation confirms the viewer and commenter block. It does not cover shared drive settings or data loss prevention rules. So an admin rule may block the download even when your role looks right.
If you own the file, check the sharing settings first. If you do not, send the owner a short message. Ask for Editor access, or ask them to change the download setting.
A worked example: a budget tracker with several tabs
Say you keep a budget tracker. It has a Summary tab, a Monthly tab and a Notes tab. Some Notes cells hold long pasted text, and the Summary totals pull from the Monthly tab.

Download it as Microsoft Excel (.xlsx) from File, then Download. Open the file in Excel and check each part. Confirm the Summary totals still calculate, the Monthly tab has its data, and the long Notes cells are complete.
If a total shows an error, look at the formula in Excel. If a note is cut off, the cell probably went past the character limit. Fix the source in Sheets, then download again.
Do not edit the old Excel file and assume it matches Sheets. Treat the Google file as the working copy, and download a fresh file each time you need one.
Common mistakes with this download

items: Downloading a PDF by mistake. Print can send a PDF, so read the format name before you click.
Editing the Excel file and expecting Sheets to change. The download is a snapshot of one moment.
Skipping the formula check. QUERY functions and Sparklines are the ones the third-party guide names.
Downloading right after a big edit. Give Sheets a moment to save to Drive first.
Assuming all tabs came across. Count them in Excel before you rely on the file.
Trying from a view-only link. Your role decides what the File menu allows.

blocks.text: Choosing between Excel, PDF, and a copy in Sheets
Pick Excel when the next person will edit in Excel. Pick PDF when the goal is a fixed page to print or send. Pick a copy when you want to keep working in Google Sheets.
Make a copy lives in the File menu, and Google's shortcut list has no key for it. Use the menu, then open the new file to keep working.

If you only need a few cells, copy them from Sheets and paste them into Excel. That skips the file check, and it does not carry tabs or settings across. Use the full download when you need the whole workbook.
Next steps after your download

If the data came from several sources, duplicate rows may show up. Read [how to remove duplicate rows in Google Sheets on Mac](/how-to/remove-duplicate-rows-in-google-sheets) before you share the file.

Need an older version before you export? Check the file's history first, then download the version you need. The steps are in [how to see revision history in Google Sheets on Mac](/how-to/see-revision-history-in-google-sheets).
Keep the Google file as the source for the next round of edits. Repeat the download only when someone needs an Excel copy. That habit keeps one version of the truth.

faq.question: Does Google Sheets have a Mac app I can export from?
faq.answer: Google Sheets is a web app, and a third-party Mac guide says there is no native Mac app. Use the browser version. The steps in this guide match the current web version as of November 7, 2026.

faq.question: Why does my menu say Download as, not Download?
faq.answer: Google's official help writes Download as. Some guides and menus show just Download. Both lead to the same list of formats, so pick Microsoft Excel (.xlsx) from that list.

faq.question: Do my formulas survive the download?
faq.answer: The Bricks guide says QUERY functions and some Sparklines may not convert. Check those cells in Excel after the download, because errors may show up there.

faq.question: Can I download only one tab as Excel?
faq.answer: Google's pages do not say whether the Excel download includes all tabs. Some third-party guides say it does. To keep one tab, copy it into a new Google Sheets file and download that file.

faq.question: Why is the download greyed out on a file someone shared with me?
faq.answer: You probably have Viewer or Commenter access. The Bricks guide says that usually means your account lacks Editor access. Ask the owner for Editor access.

faq.question: How do I get a PDF instead of an Excel file on a Mac?
faq.answer: Use File, then Print, or press ⌘P. Choose Workbook, Selected cells or Current sheet, then click Next. Chrome opens a print window, and Firefox or Safari download a PDF.

faq.question: Is there a size limit for the download?
faq.answer: Drive help says a spreadsheet can hold up to 20 million cells or 100 MB. Google's September 10, 2026 post raised the cell limit from 10 million to 20 million.

faq.question: Does the Excel file update when I change the sheet?
faq.answer: No. The file is a copy from the moment you downloaded it. Download again after you make changes, and keep the Google file as the working copy.

faq.question: Can I follow these steps on Windows?
faq.answer: Google's help pages say the File menu is the same on a Mac as on Windows. The same menu steps should work there, but this page is written for the Mac.

steps.name: Open the file with Editor access
steps.text: Open the spreadsheet in your browser, from Google Drive or from a link you were sent. Check that your role is Editor or Owner. A Viewer or Commenter may not see the Download option at all.
steps.tip: Not sure of your role? Open the Share settings to see it.

steps.name: Open the File menu
steps.text: Click File in the Sheets menu bar, just under the file name. You can also press ⌃⌥F, the Mac shortcut Google lists for the File menu.
steps.tip: Google writes this as Ctrl + Option + F. On a Mac, Ctrl is ⌃.

steps.name: Hover over Download
steps.text: In the File menu, move the pointer to Download. Google's help pages call this item Download as. Move slowly to the right so the submenu stays open.

steps.name: Pick Microsoft Excel (.xlsx)
steps.text: In the submenu, click Microsoft Excel (.xlsx). Google's official page does not name Excel in this step, but the list of formats is where you find it. The browser starts the download.
steps.tip: Do not pick PDF if you need an Excel file.

steps.name: Find the file in Downloads
steps.text: Open Finder, click Downloads in the sidebar, and look for the .xlsx file. The name usually matches the spreadsheet title. If it is not there, check your browser's download list.
steps.tip: The Bricks guide says the browser saves the file to the Downloads folder.

steps.name: Open it in Excel and check it
steps.text: Open the .xlsx in Excel for Mac or another spreadsheet app. Check every tab, every formula that uses QUERY or Sparklines, and any long text cell. Compare the file with the Google Sheets version.
steps.tip: Keep the Google Sheets file as the source. Edits in Excel do not sync back.

shortcuts.action: Print, or make a PDF instead of Excel

troubleshooting.problem: Download as Excel is greyed out
troubleshooting.fix: Ask the owner for Editor access. Owners can turn off downloads for viewers and commenters, so ask them to check the sharing settings.

troubleshooting.problem: The .xlsx file is not in Downloads
troubleshooting.fix: Check your browser's download list first. It shows where the file went. If it is missing, retry the download after you confirm it did not save elsewhere.

troubleshooting.problem: QUERY or Sparkline cells show errors in Excel
troubleshooting.fix: The Bricks guide says QUERY functions and some Sparklines may not convert. Rebuild those cells in Excel, or keep the Google file as the source and paste values.

troubleshooting.problem: Text in one cell is cut off in the Excel file
troubleshooting.fix: Drive help says cells with more than 50,000 characters are removed when a file is converted. Shorten the text in Sheets, then download again.

troubleshooting.problem: Sheets will not hold all the data you need
troubleshooting.fix: Drive help lists a limit of 20 million cells or 100 MB per spreadsheet. Split the work into separate files by period, region or client.

troubleshooting.problem: A tab is missing from the Excel file
troubleshooting.fix: Some third-party guides say all tabs come across, and Google's pages do not confirm it. Count tabs in both files. The fix in third-party guides is to copy the missing tab into a new Google Sheets file, then download that file.
